rationale.core_concept: Management of hyperkalemia in a patient with acute on chronic kidney failure.
rationale.answer_analysis: In a patient with severe hyperkalemia and ECG changes (peaked T-waves), the immediate priority is to stabilize the cardiac cell membrane to prevent life-threatening arrhythmias. Intravenous calcium gluconate works rapidly to antagonize the cardiac effects of hyperkalemia without lowering serum potassium levels. While insulin and dextrose will shift potassium intracellularly, and sodium polystyrene sulfonate will remove potassium from the body, these take longer to act and do not provide immediate cardiac protection. Hemodialysis is the most effective way to remove potassium but is not the first-line intervention for immediate cardiac stabilization.
